theorem_title: Coprime-to-three powers cannot divide a normalized odd content
natural_language_statement:
Let $d,Q,K,R,H,p,E\in\mathbb N$. Assume $H$ is odd, $p>1$, $\gcd(p,3)=1$, $E>0$, and the leading-coefficient equality

$$2^R3^{dQ}=2^{dK}H.$$

Then

$$p^E\nmid H.$$

Equivalently, adding the divisibility hypothesis $p^E\mid H$ makes these assumptions inconsistent, which is the form proved in Lean. No primality assumption on $p$ is needed. This checks the arithmetic core of the normalized-content obstruction; the resonant base $3$ is outside its coprimality hypothesis.
